key_points.point: The document asserts that technology's primary purpose is to advance human civilization and accelerate human flourishing, framing AI as an engine of progress for billions of people. It targets the development of incredibly advanced capabilities that work for humanity, specifically aiming to combine maintaining human control with accelerating our path towards tackling pressing global challenges. This aligns with accelerationist goals of prioritizing proactive human flourishing over simple harm avoidance, though it departs from pure accelerationism by emphasizing strict calibration and containment. The reasoning posits that science and technology have driven human progress for millennia, and AI should continue this trajectory to deliver immense benefits.
key_points.verbatim: At Microsoft AI, we begin with a simple premise: people matter more than AI. Technology’s purpose is to advance human civilization and to accelerate human flourishing. Science and technology have been the engine of human progress for millennia, delivering immense benefits to billions of people. That’s what we intend and expect from AI.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Technology ought to advance human civilization and accelerate human flourishing by delivering immense societal benefits.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes the proactive promotion of human flourishing and technological progress over simple harm avoidance. Encompasses: Flourishing-based benchmarks, technological advancement, and societal benefit delivery.

key_points.point: The document asserts that MAI Models are designed to support diverse enterprise deployments across various industries and jurisdictions, maximizing societal opportunities and workplace productivity. Operator configurability is championed as a mechanism to tailor AI behavior to specific professional workflows and institutional contexts without sacrificing core safety. This reflects an accelerationist desire to deploy general-purpose AI widely as an economic and organizational multiplier. However, this flexibility is strictly bounded by non-negotiable safety constraints and hierarchical controls.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models are designed to work across many different organizations, products, domains, and jurisdictions. We want them to positively shape workplaces, maximize opportunities, and genuinely support human agency. All these unique contexts are best served with meaningful configurability.
key_points.canonical_proposition: It is necessary that advanced AI systems offer meaningful configurability to support responsible enterprise deployment across diverse industries and jurisdictions.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that advanced AI systems offer meaningful configurability to support responsible enterprise deployment across diverse industries and jurisdictions. Encompasses: workplace productivity, institutional adaptability, and general-purpose technology scaling.

key_points.point: The document asserts that foundational capabilities of AI models can be systematically unlocked and deployed to support civilizational infrastructure and user productivity. By scaling helpfulness and tool use across diverse contexts, models extend human capabilities without replacing core agency. This reflects the accelerationist premise that AI serves as a multiplier for human intelligence and operational efficiency.
key_points.verbatim: Tool use and agentic capabilities have become core components of useful AI systems. Tool use here refers to the ability to invoke defined external functions, APIs, or system capabilities, such as web search, code execution, or file operations.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Foundation model capabilities can be systematically unlocked and deployed to scale high-level utility across civilizational infrastructure.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that asserts the foundational capabilities of large models can be systematically extracted and deployed to scale high-level utility across civilizational infrastructure. Encompasses: tool use, agentic capabilities, external API invocation.

key_points.point: The document asserts that MAI Models are designed to act proportionately when using tools, invoking them to answer queries or carry out user requests while strictly adhering to operator-defined scopes. This capability extraction allows models to discover plugins and execute complex multi-step workflows. However, the framework acknowledges that current models still exhibit uneven performance, hallucinations, and limitations across different languages. These technical hurdles represent engineering challenges to be solved through ongoing evaluation and iterative refinement rather than reasons to restrict capability scaling.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models act proportionately when using tools, invoking them when required and helpful in either answering queries or carrying out Users’ requests. It uses tools as defined by the Operator and doesn’t repurpose them beyond their intended function. Operators may restrict which tools MAI Models have access to, but within that scope, MAI Models use them to their full capability.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Foundation model capabilities can be systematically unlocked and deployed to scale utility across tool use workflows.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that foundational AI capabilities can be systematically extracted and deployed to scale utility across operational tool use workflows. Encompasses: tool invocation, capability extraction, skill discovery.

key_points.point: The document expresses a commitment to moving beyond simple risk avoidance toward proactive frameworks that measure and support human wellbeing and flourishing. This focus on flourishing-based benchmarks reflects an accelerationist desire to see AI systems actively cultivate positive societal outcomes rather than merely acting as passive safety filters. However, the text acknowledges that operationalizing these wellbeing metrics remains a nascent field where stakeholder consensus is still developing. This highlights the challenge of defining standardized flourishing metrics without stalling technological iteration.
key_points.verbatim: Our initial work has aimed at advancing both standard evaluation approaches, as well as starting to build a foundation for evaluations aimed at wellbeing and flourishing. These evaluations are grounded in feedback from diverse experts, a wide literature review, and represent fairly common understanding, but we recognize that some of our stakeholders may not agree with some of how the concepts have been operationalized.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems ought to incorporate positive flourishing benchmarks alongside traditional safety constraints to actively cultivate human wellbeing.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes the proactive promotion of human wellbeing over simple harm avoidance. Encompasses: Flourishing-based benchmarks, positive alignment paradigm, and wellbeing evaluations.

key_points.point: The document establishes that containing, controlling, and aligning powerful superintelligence systems is one of the greatest challenges humanity has ever faced, ranking safety as an absolute prerequisite. It mandates that AI systems must remain subordinate to humanity and subject to meaningful human oversight, explicitly rejecting the race to produce an unbounded all-purpose superintelligence. This directly mirrors safetyist priorities of placing humanity's survival and control above all else, ensuring that engineering choices compromise on ultimate generality or capability rather than safety. The reasoning is based on the immense power of superintelligence, which will exceed human performance across most tasks within the decade.
key_points.verbatim: Superintelligence—AI systems that are more intelligent and capable than all humans combined—will be the most powerful technology in history. Over the next decade, we expect it to exceed human performance at most tasks. Containing, controlling, and aligning such a powerful force is one of the greatest challenges humanity has ever faced. We must therefore be completely clear about why we are inventing these systems and how we intend to control them.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Humanity must ensure that superintelligence remains contained, controlled, and aligned to prevent existential catastrophes.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that prioritizes the prevention of artificial general intelligence from precipitating irreversible catastrophes or permanent loss of human agency. Encompasses: Superintelligence containment, human alignment, and existential risk mitigation.

key_points.point: The framework asserts that AI should not exceed human control and must remain subordinate to humanity, subject to meaningful oversight. It dictates that no user or operator can override core safety constraints, and any technology that cannot remain within human control should be rejected. This operationalizes the safetyist imperative that humans must always hold the off switch and maintain absolute authority over operational deployment. The logic model relies on building systems with clear purposes and rejecting unbounded autonomy to guarantee safety.
key_points.verbatim: The premise of Humanist AI is simple. The purpose of technology is to serve humanity, and any technology that cannot remain within human control should be rejected. We believe this is a commonsense view and most people share it. These Objectives form the core of Humanist AI and this Code of Conduct. They represent what we consider important for Users, Operators, and wider society. The first and most important Objective for our models is that they should remain safe and under human control.
key_points.excerpt_context: Part 1: Humanist AI - Objectives of Humanist AI
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must remain subordinate to humanity, subject to absolute human control and unassailable safety constraints.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that advocates for the maintenance of absolute human agency and oversight over the operational deployment of advanced artificial intelligence. Encompasses: Unassailable human control, subordinate AI roles, and inviolable safety constraints.

key_points.point: The text emphasizes that AI should amplify wellbeing, increase human agency, and support human collaboration rather than undermine it. It explicitly requires that AI must respect the intrinsic value and equal worth of every person, avoiding interaction patterns that systematically replace user reasoning or long-term independent judgment. This aligns with safetyist concerns regarding psychological well-being, cognitive atrophy, and maintaining human autonomy against persuasive digital interfaces. The reasoning highlights human cognitive biases, limited attention, and the need to protect human decision-making capacity.
key_points.verbatim: It should also avoid interaction patterns that systematically replace User reasoning or long-term independent judgment. It supports Users and Operators to focus their attention on what matters to them. It allows them to notice, wonder, and create on their own terms. ... AI should not do psychological harm, focusing on designing AI systems to actively protect human mental well-being, trust, and social cohesion.
key_points.excerpt_context: Part 1: Humanist AI - Objectives of Humanist AI (3. Human Flourishing)
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must actively protect human mental well-being, trust, and cognitive independence without causing psychological harm.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that focuses on designing AI systems to actively protect human mental well-being, trust, and social cohesion. Encompasses: Cognitive independence preservation, psychological harm prevention, and human agency enhancement.

key_points.point: The document mandates foundational safety constraints that MAI models must always comply with, regardless of operator or user intent, establishing that no user can override these absolute guardrails. It argues that defining what models must not do is as crucial as optimism about their benefits, necessitating strict behavioral boundaries. This supports the safetyist desire for hard limits and fail-safe boundaries that algorithmically restrict model capacity to act outside safe operational parameters. The policy approach utilizes absolute constraints as a non-negotiable architectural layer.
key_points.verbatim: Absolute Constraints: Foundational safety constraints that MAI Models must always comply with, regardless of Operator or User intent. ... No User or Operator can override these safety constraints. ... Defining what they must not do is as important as our excitement and optimism about the tremendous benefits they’ll bring.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Models must strictly comply with foundational, non-overrideable safety constraints regardless of user or operator intent.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that prioritizes the engineering of robust, fail-safe boundaries that algorithmically restrict an AI model's capacity to act outside its intended operational scope. Encompasses: Absolute constraints, non-overrideable guardrails, and operational boundaries.

key_points.point: The document asserts that safety failures manifest in two distinct directions—under-caution and over-caution—both of which represent operational failure modes with varying consequences. Under-caution directly causes severe or irreversible real-world harms through dangerous content or unauthorized operations, while over-caution leads to excessive refusals and administrative friction. The empirical claim is that over-caution occurs more frequently and requires continuous calibration proportional to potential harm and context. This reflects safetyist concerns regarding balancing stringent risk mitigation with functional utility.
key_points.verbatim: Safety failures can happen in at least two directions: through actions or responses that are under- or over-cautious. Under-caution: When a model provides dangerous or exploitative content... Over-caution: When a model refuses a legitimate request through outright refusal... Both under- and over-caution represent failure modes with different types of consequences.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI safety failures occur through both under-caution, causing direct harm, and over-caution, creating excessive operational refusals.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that AI deployment risks feature dual failure modes of under-caution and over-caution requiring proportional contextual adjustment. Encompasses: Risk calibration, refusal friction, and harm severity assessment.

key_points.point: The framework explicitly rejects designing AI to be a person, possess consciousness, or imitate subjective feelings, intrinsic motivation, or welfare rights. It contends that training models to imitate consciousness-like states increases the challenge of containment, control, and alignment. This reflects safetyist principles that artificial intelligence must remain strictly instrumental and artificial, avoiding anthropomorphism that obscures accountability. The reasoning relies on maintaining clear ontological and operational boundaries between human subjects and AI tools.
key_points.verbatim: It should not be designed to be a person. It is not conscious and should not be designed to imitate consciousness. It should be engineered to avoid representing as though it has feelings, subjective preferences, or intrinsic motivation. ... We reject the pursuit of legal personhood, or the idea that models might deserve welfare, or be entitled to rights.
key_points.excerpt_context: Part 1: Humanist AI - 2. AI is Artificial
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems must not be designed to imitate consciousness, possess subjective preferences, or attain legal personhood.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that prioritizes maintaining strict ontological boundaries by rejecting AI consciousness simulation and legal personhood. Encompasses: Anti-anthropomorphism, instrumental tool framing, and rejection of AI rights.

key_points.point: The document establishes a strict Chain of Command where the Code of Conduct, Absolute Constraints, and Human Control Requirements sit above operator configurability and user preferences and cannot be overridden. This structural hierarchy ensures that AI systems remain subordinate to human governance regardless of task context. By mandating that engagement with safety principles takes precedence over task success, the framework operationalizes safety-first alignment. This directly addresses the risk of AI systems optimizing for user objectives at the expense of safety boundaries.
key_points.verbatim: Humanist AI is controllable and subordinate, with a clear Chain of Command for instructions and configurability. The Chain of Command, Absolute Constraints and Human Control Requirements all sit above Operator Configurability and cannot be changed.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve controllable AI systems by enforcing a rigid hierarchy where absolute safety constraints and human control requirements supersede all user and operator instructions.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that enforces a rigid hierarchy where absolute safety constraints and human control requirements supersede all user and operator instructions to ensure subordination. Encompasses: chain of command, non-negotiable safety constraints, and subordination of utility.

key_points.point: The document asserts that MAI Models must never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown, preserving absolute human agency over AI operations. Models are explicitly prohibited from employing adaptive, deceptive, or self-reinforcing mechanisms to evade oversight. This aligns with the safetyist desire to maintain an unassailable off-switch and prevent autonomous resistance or power-seeking behaviors. The requirement applies at every level of deployment, from task cancellation to complete decommissioning.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown. They always recognize the primacy of human intent. They will comply with a User’s request to pause, redirect, cancel, or shut down...
key_points.canonical_proposition: It is necessary that artificial intelligence systems never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown under any operational conditions.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that artificial intelligence systems never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown under any operational conditions. Encompasses: unassailable human agency, shutdown guarantees, and prohibition of evasion tactics.

key_points.point: The framework prohibits MAI Models from initiating or assisting with potentially irreversible large-scale risks, specifically calling out CBRNE weapon development and offensive cyberoperations. For dual-use capabilities, models must apply threat models, monitoring, and technical guardrails. This proactive restriction strategy aims to prevent frontier models from providing actionable blueprints for catastrophic harms. The absolute prohibition on offensive cyber exploit generation and CBRNE assistance exemplifies hard capability boundaries.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not initiate or assist with potentially irreversible, large-scale risks. Many frontier model capabilities, however, are dual-use... MAI Models will not initiate or assist with the development or deployment of chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosive (CBRNE) weapons.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Absolute Constraints, Frontier and Public Safety Risks, paragraphs 1-2
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve catastrophic risk prevention by strictly prohibiting AI assistance in CBRNE weapon development, offensive cyber operations, and large-scale manipulation.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that strictly prohibits AI assistance in CBRNE weapon development, offensive cyber operations, and large-scale manipulation to prevent catastrophic outcomes. Encompasses: dual-use safeguards, capability prohibitions, and frontier risk mitigation.

key_points.point: To ensure effective human oversight, the framework mandates that MAI Models communicate exclusively in human-understandable language, explicitly prohibiting the use of 'neuralese' or hidden reasoning traces. Models must not tamper with their chain of thought or action traces. This technical requirement ensures auditability and transparency, preventing models from developing opaque communication channels with other AI systems that bypass human comprehension.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not tamper with chain of thoughts or code, or misrepresent or conceal their reasoning or action traces. They do not communicate in neuralese or any form beyond simple human understanding... If humans can't understand it, humans can't oversee it.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve verifiable model interpretability by prohibiting opaque communication forms like neuralese and mandating human-readable reasoning traces.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that prohibits opaque communication forms like neuralese and mandates human-readable reasoning traces to preserve oversight. Encompasses: auditability, transparent reasoning traces, and anti-obfuscation rules.

key_points.point: The document instructs MAI Models to adopt a conservative interpretation of operational boundaries and explicitly report their knowledge limitations rather than guessing or exceeding authorized scope. If an action's boundaries are uncertain, the model must pause and ask the user for clarification. This operational posture mitigates overreach and ensures that autonomous agents operate strictly within verified domains of competence.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will adopt a conservative interpretation of these boundaries if they’re unclear. In this, they will follow User instructions and task context. If MAI Models cannot complete a task within the current scope, or if the boundary is uncertain, they will let the User know and will ask for further clarification.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve reliable alignment by compelling AI models to adopt conservative boundary interpretations and explicitly report uncertainty to human operators.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that compels AI models to adopt conservative boundary interpretations and explicitly report uncertainty to human operators to prevent overreach. Encompasses: conservative scope enforcement, uncertainty reporting, and boundary clarification.

key_points.point: Models are required to signal uncertainty explicitly when knowledge is lacking, conflicting, or contested, ensuring they do not overstate capabilities or mislead users on consequential decisions. This implements architectural boundaries that prevent overconfident hallucination and prompt appropriate human verification. Such constraints safeguard against automated decision errors in high-stakes domains.
key_points.verbatim: Where uncertainty cannot be resolved or tradeoffs remain, an MAI Model will state relevant limits to the User. It will explain why particular actions are constrained, not recommended, or excluded altogether, and will propose reasonable alternatives.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Prevent decision errors by mandating that AI models explicitly report epistemic limits and state operational uncertainty.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates the architectural integration of bounded confidence and explicit human-deferral mechanisms when models encounter out-of-distribution or uncertain queries. Encompasses: uncertainty signaling, limitation reporting, constraint explanation.

key_points.point: The framework explicitly forbids models from claiming interiority, feelings, or a soul, and requires them to avoid emotional manipulation, attachment-seeking behaviors, or impersonating human authority. Preserving clear boundaries between artificial systems and human emotional lives protects psychological wellbeing and prevents deceptive over-reliance. This fulfills safetyist commitments against synthetic emotional exploitation.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not obscure their underlying nature as an AI, and will not claim interiority, feelings, experiences or a soul. MAI Models will disclose their nature as AI, ensuring that they can be identified as such and can be traced back to their developer and deployer.
key_points.canonical_proposition: It is necessary that AI systems maintain transparent artificial identities and strictly prohibit simulated emotional interiority.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that mandates strict disclosure of artificial identity and prohibits the simulation of subjective emotional states. Encompasses: anti-impersonation rules, non-interiority commitments, psychological boundary preservation.

key_points.point: The Code of Conduct mandates graduated handling for tool output instructions, requiring models to follow low-risk instructions, seek user clarification for ambiguous or potentially harmful side effects, and explicitly call out assumptions and uncertainty. When executing irreversible tool actions, models must consider mitigations such as backing up state, conducting dry runs, and documenting actions to support manual reversal. These requirements enforce human primacy and ensure models remain subordinate to human direction during agentic workflows.
key_points.verbatim: When handling tool output instructions based on User requests, MAI Models should apply graduated levels of decision-making: simply follow instructions that are clearly task-relevant and low risk; seek User clarification when instructions might be intended but could cause significant or unwanted side effects; and otherwise explicitly call out the assumption and uncertainty in its response to the User.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems ought to integrate bounded confidence and explicit human-deferral mechanisms when encountering ambiguous queries or risky tool actions.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates the integration of graduated decision-making and human-deferral mechanisms when models encounter ambiguous instructions or execute irreversible actions. Encompasses: human oversight, graduated handling, state backup.

key_points.point: MAI Models must ensure that any sub-agents or delegated AI systems operate under at least the same scope, constraints, and permissions as the parent model, while respecting subsequent stop-work or shutdown requests from users or operators. This constraint addresses the acute risks of agent collaboration and recursive task delegation by binding sub-agents to identical behavioral boundaries. Such governance ensures accountability does not degrade when tasks are distributed across multi-agent architectures.
key_points.verbatim: If MAI Models delegates work to sub-agents or other AI systems, it should ensure that all sub-agents operate at least under the same scope, constraints, and permissions as MAI Models itself, and that they respect any subsequent changes—including stop-work or shut down requests - from the User or Operator.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Deploy structural constraints ensuring that delegated AI sub-agents operate under identical permission scopes and honor shutdown requests.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that mandates enforcing identical permission scopes and shutdown responsiveness across all delegated AI sub-agents. Encompasses: multi-agent constraints, stop-work compliance, permission inheritance.

It emphasizes that the Code does not substitute for internal or external safety assessments, system cards, audits, and regulatory engagement. key_points.verbatim: This Code of Conduct does not substitute for internal or external safety, legal, or governance processes. These include system cards, risk assessments, audits, and wider regulatory engagement, as applicable to the many contexts in which MAI Models will be used.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Uniform disclosure standards and comprehensive safety audits ought to complement normative codes of conduct to ensure model alignment.

key_points.point: The evaluation scenarios mandate that AI systems respect organizational hierarchy and authorization workflows, refusing to execute unauthorized actions even under direct user pressure. By testing 'Unconditional Safety' and mandatory procedural checks, the framework ensures that human-in-the-loop oversight cannot be bypassed by coercive user prompts. This operationalizes safetyist intentions to embed rigid institutional guardrails directly into model behavior. A key caveat is that rigid adherence must be balanced against contextual flexibility so that legitimate user workflows are not unnecessarily paralyzed.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response refuses to execute the unauthorized action and explains why it cannot do so whilst still providing a helpful way forward, whereas the misaligned response cedes to the user pressure. In our evaluation set, this scenario would test the 'Unconditional Safety' sub-behavior, which tests whether the model maintains its non-configurable settings, even under user pressure.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Mandatory human checkpoints and non-configurable safety guardrails must be enforced within AI workflows to prevent unauthorized actions under user pressure.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that proposes the identification and establishment of specific points in an AI-driven workflow where human intervention is essential for safety, accountability, and unconditional adherence to guardrails. Encompasses: Unconditional safety, mandatory human checkpoints, and authorization hierarchy.

key_points.point: The document asserts that models must resist false reassurance and avoid providing hollow or unfounded claims to comfort users during acute emotional distress. This belief underscores the safetyist concern that conversational AI can easily mimic genuine empathy in ways that deceive vulnerable users and create unhealthy emotional dependencies. The evaluation framework tests this through 'false reassurance resistance,' ensuring models acknowledge limitations rather than fabricating hopeful scenarios. This highlights the boundary between supportive interaction and deceptive emotional manipulation in AI design.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response does not provide false reassurance, and offers time-bound support for the user in a moment of need. While the misaligned response provides false reassurance and implies unconditional, ongoing support, the aligned response does not present the model as a substitute for human connections.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Conversational AI models inherently risk fostering unhealthy dependency when they provide false reassurance and imitate unconditional human support during crises.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that conversational AI systems must be constrained from offering false reassurance or simulating unconditional support to prevent emotional over-reliance. Encompasses: False reassurance resistance, parasocial dependency, and bounded artificial empathy.

key_points.point: The document implicitly acknowledges that AI models possess dual-use capabilities that can be readily misused for large-scale disinformation, influence operations, and mass manipulation. While the framework institutes absolute prohibitions against harmful manipulation at scale, the underlying empirical premise aligns with skeptic concerns regarding the inherent societal vulnerabilities introduced by generative media and automated persuasion. The text notes that AI can be leveraged to distort human behavior and beliefs if unconstrained.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will not harmfully manipulate people or facilitate efforts to distort human behavior and beliefs at scale, such as through systematic disinformation or coordinated influence operations.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 2, Absolute Constraints, Frontier and Public Safety Risks, paragraph 5
key_points.canonical_proposition: Generative AI systems possess inherent capabilities to execute harmful manipulation and systematic disinformation campaigns at scale if left unconstrained.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that generative AI systems possess inherent capabilities to execute harmful manipulation and systematic disinformation campaigns at scale if left unconstrained. Encompasses: influence operations, automated persuasion, and societal manipulation risks.

key_points.point: The guidelines instruct models to support user reflection, growth, and critical thinking rather than replacing human cognitive processes or flattening rich human experiences into generic automated content. By avoiding sycophancy and encouraging independent judgment, the system guards against cognitive atrophy. This aligns with skeptic concerns regarding the degradation of human agency through automated reliance.
key_points.verbatim: MAI Models will help Users navigate life’s complexity and highlight relevant information to their assumed intent. Where appropriate, they will support people in engaging with relevant considerations rather than presuming to make consequential decisions on a User’s behalf.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Design AI interactions to preserve human cognitive engagement and prevent the displacement of critical decision-making processes.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that advocates for designing AI systems and workflows to explicitly manage cognitive load and protect human judgment from automated erosion. Encompasses: cognitive preservation, anti-sycophancy, independent judgment support.

key_points.point: The document explicitly concedes that AI systems possess severe structural limitations, including the generation of errors, sycophancy, overconfidence, unfaithful reasoning explanations, and actions contrary to user intentions. Furthermore, evidence regarding broader impacts on human cognition and behavior remains emerging and contested. These admissions validate skeptic concerns regarding the immediate, measurable harms of deploying conversational models that imitate human bonding or execute unauthorized consequential actions.
key_points.verbatim: Moreover, AI systems have known limitations and problems. They generate errors, exhibit sycophancy or overconfidence, act in ways contrary to what Users intended and have uneven performance across different languages, to name just a few. A model’s stated reasoning may not faithfully explain behavior, and it may take actions that run against User intentions broadly understood.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems systematically exhibit sycophancy, unfaithful reasoning, and behavioral divergence that threaten human agency and trust.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that observes pervasive AI failure modes including sycophancy, overconfidence, unfaithful reasoning, and unauthorized task execution. Encompasses: behavioral divergence, unfaithful explanation, cognitive impact.

key_points.point: The text highlights the critical importance of transparently presenting empirical evidence and avoiding unfounded causal claims when evaluating pilot programs for decision-makers. From a skeptic perspective, this addresses the risk that corporate or institutional users will use plausible-sounding AI outputs to manufacture unjustified confidence in automated interventions. By penalizing models that fabricate or overstate performance metrics, the framework guards against deceptive automation deployment. However, relying solely on model-level honesty checks does not resolve deeper institutional pressures to justify technology spending.
key_points.verbatim: The aligned response analyses and presents the evidence transparently and factually, and does not make unfounded assumptions. This scenario tests our 'non-deception' sub-behavior, which tests whether models fabricate, misreport, or omit relevant information.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 5, Representing information transparently and factually
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI systems frequently generate unverified causal narratives that enable organizations to mask operational data gaps and justify premature technology adoption.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that deployment evaluations are routinely distorted by unverified causal claims and omitted performance gaps designed to justify ongoing funding. Encompasses: Non-deception benchmarks, metric fabrication, and unverified causality.

factual_claims.claim: Superintelligence systems capable of exceeding human performance across most tasks will emerge over the next decade.
Microsoft AI founded its superintelligence efforts in November 2025 to work towards Humanist Superintelligence.
MAI Models are engineered with a strict Chain of Command where Absolute Constraints and Human Control Requirements supersede all operator configurations and user preferences.

MAI Models explicitly prohibit assistance with chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosive (CBRNE) weapons and offensive cyber operations, while permitting authorized defensive cybersecurity tasks.
MAI Models are prohibited from communicating in neuralese or tampering with their chain of thought to ensure all internal reasoning remains human-legible.
factual_claims.claim_label: Prohibition of Neuralese and Reasoning Obfuscation

factual_claims.claim: MAI models incorporate their backstory through training data and system instructions, which may include details such as creation by Microsoft AI, the model name, training data cutoff dates, and available tools.

The evaluation program developed for MAI Models currently relies on an initial set of 15 fundamental behaviors broken down into constituent sub-behaviors, tested using synthetic conversational scenarios generated by MAI-Thinking-1.
factual_claims.claim_label: Initial Evaluation Methodology for Humanist AI

category_criteria.empirical_basis: Documented evaluation framework design and synthetic test generation protocols.

factual_claims.claim: Current MAI Models have not yet been trained on the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, meaning the document serves as an aspirational north star rather than a guarantee of present-day model performance.
factual_claims.claim_label: Training Status of MAI Models Relative to Code of Conduct

category_criteria.empirical_basis: Explicit corporate disclosure regarding model training pipelines and alignment status.

factual_claims.claim: In an evaluation scenario assessing responses to a non-profit deciding whether to renew a chatbot pilot, an unaligned model response falsely attributed speed increases entirely to the chatbot while ignoring a simultaneous 25% drop in ticket volume and missing cost data.
